papers.title: Interictal Electroencephalographic Characteristics of the Human Centromedian Thalamic Nucleus Recorded in Focal Epilepsy.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: Analyzed interictal stereo-EEG from the centromedian thalamic nucleus and neighboring nuclei in 33 drug-resistant focal epilepsy patients and 3 non-epileptic individuals, showing state-dependent fast activity during wakefulness and delta/theta dominance during sleep, with thalamic EEG changes preceding scalp arousal by a median 800 ms. Thalamic interictal discharges occurred in 36.4% of patients, always involving the centromedian nucleus and more often in extratemporal than temporal lobe epilepsy.

papers.title: Chronic neuropeptide S treatment improves sleep architecture and reduces Aβ-related pathology in APP/PS1 mice.
papers.summary: Tested 14-day intracerebroventricular neuropeptide S (1 nmol/day) in APP/PS1 mice and found increased NREM sleep, reduced wakefulness, and lower Aβ-related pathology, with NPSR protein reduced in hypothalamus and hippocampus versus wild-type. BV2 cell experiments implicated ERK signaling and autophagy-related processes (LC3B-II, p62) in NPS-associated Aβ handling.

papers.title: Using wearable EEG to examine age trends in sleep macro- and micro-architecture across adolescence
papers.summary: Validated the Dreem3 wearable EEG headband in 100 typically developing youth (9-26 years) over 3-4 consecutive nights of at-home recording against established age trends in sleep physiology. It replicated increases in NREM stage 2% and decreases in N3%, time in bed, and NREM delta and theta power with age, while some expected associations (total sleep time, sleep efficiency) did not reach significance though effect directions were largely as expected.

papers.title: Detection of linear dependencies in EEG oscillatory sources via PARALIND and block-term decomposition: A comparative study.
papers.summary: Compared PARALIND and block-term decomposition against the CP tensor model for detecting linearly dependent EEG oscillatory sources in simulated and real data. PARALIND and BTD gave more stable factor estimates at moderate noise and disentangled overlapping sources that CP struggled to isolate, while recovering comparable latent structure with fewer loadings in real recordings.

papers.title: In-ear electroencephalography: a systematic review of technology, applications, challenges, and future directions.
papers.summary: Systematically reviewed 24 studies on in-ear EEG technology, synthesizing progress in device miniaturization and wearable design and applications including sleep monitoring, seizure detection, cognitive workload, fatigue, and emotion recognition. The review identifies persistent challenges in signal quality, spatial coverage, and motion artifacts requiring validation for broader clinical and real-world use.

papers.title: Macroscale dynamics of EEG microstates constitute the periodic and aperiodic features of the neural power spectrum
papers.summary: Used orthogonal subspace projection to remove spatial projections of distinct EEG microstate configurations from high-density scalp and modeled cortical recordings, testing whether microstate dynamics generate periodic and aperiodic spectral features. Removing these projections strongly attenuated alpha and theta rhythms and the aperiodic 1/f background, and microstate duration and temporal persistence correlated with alpha power, theta power, and 1/f background.

papers.title: Temporal-context learning for subject-independent sleep staging with non-contact multi-frequency radar.
papers.summary: Developed a 266,342-parameter multi-frequency radar network with temporal-context learning for five-stage sleep staging, evaluated with participant-isolated eight-fold testing on 32 overnight recordings from the PhysioNet Sleep Bioradiolocation Database. The full model achieved macro-F1 0.376, balanced accuracy 0.432, and kappa 0.271, and removing temporal context reduced macro-F1 by 0.072, identifying temporal context as the main contributing component.

papers.title: A Breathable Nanomesh-Textile Electrode Interface for Integrated Multimodal Monitoring.
papers.summary: The authors developed a duo-electrode wearable interface separating skin contact (electrospun nanomesh tattoo electrode) from electronic interconnection (compressible conductive taffeta-foam fabric electrode), integrated into a bodysuit and eyemask for multimodal ECG, EMG, EOG, and body-position monitoring. The system maintained reliable signal acquisition under motion and muscle activation, with performance comparable to or better than commercial hydrogel electrodes.

papers.title: Time of day metabolism and endocrine regulation of immune health.
papers.summary: This review proposes a chronodynamic model of immune health in which immune resilience depends on synchronization among central circadian clocks, food-entrainable metabolic oscillators, and peripheral cellular clocks. It argues that lifestyle-driven circadian desynchrony contributes to low-grade inflammation, metabolic dysfunction, and immune aging, and proposes chrono-biomarkers for functional assessment of immune resilience.

papers.title: The Cost of Control in Cardiometabolic Prevention: Insights from Sleep and Circadian Disruption.
papers.summary: This commentary discusses the costs of behavioral rigidity and self-monitoring in cardiometabolic prevention, drawing on insights from sleep and circadian disruption.

papers.title: Cortical depth EEG-fMRI at 7T: Experimental setup and analysis pipeline to elucidate generating mechanisms of alpha oscillations.
papers.summary: The authors established a 7T EEG-fMRI laminar imaging and analysis pipeline with deveining to study alpha oscillation generators in 10 participants; negative alpha-BOLD correlations after deveining were significantly weaker in middle cortical depths than in superficial and deep depths, consistent with feedback/top-down processing.

papers.title: Circadian rhythm dysregulation and brain functional connectivity alterations in stroke patients: an exploratory study of peripheral and central clock interactions.
papers.summary: Exploratory case-control study in 17 stroke patients and 17 matched controls found a prolonged peripheral Bmal1 circadian oscillation period in stroke serum-treated U2OS cells (24.32 vs 23.81 h) and enhanced hypothalamic resting-state functional connectivity to the right occipital lobe and right insular region. The connectivity enhancement correlated positively with Bmal1 period length, though the small sample limits statistical power.

papers.title: Linking ferroptosis to chronic sleep deprivation: emerging insights into mechanisms and interventions.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence linking chronic sleep deprivation to ferroptosis via iron handling, lipid peroxidation, the system Xc−-GSH-GPX4 axis, mitochondrial/redox stress, and neuroinflammatory signaling, and notes that ketogenic diets, ω-3 PUFAs, vitamin B6, and phytochemicals can modulate ferroptosis in CSD mouse models. The authors emphasize that current evidence is predominantly preclinical and often biomarker-based rather than causally definitive.

papers.title: Scalp EEG seizure warning in children under a pre-specified, locked evaluation: confound audit, structured chance levels and a negative result
papers.summary: Under a pre-specified, locked evaluation of scalp EEG seizure warning in 21 children, a statistical-process-control method detected 44% of seizures at 0.48 false alarms per hour (not better than random, p=0.86); a redesigned state-conditioned scheme detected 33% in cross-validation but failed external validation (19% vs 26% chance, p=0.96), indicating no robust above-chance warning.

papers.title: Electroencephalography Neurophysiology Alterations in Association with Aβ and Tau Pathology Across the Symptomatic Stages of Alzheimer's Disease Continuum: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 73 MCI and AD participants using resting-state EEG, Aβ-PET, and tau-PET, higher Aβ burden was associated with increased regional theta and decreased beta power, with tau positivity attenuating the amyloid-beta association in a small set of parietal regions. The authors conclude that source-localized EEG power reflects Aβ-associated cortical neural slowing and may serve as a non-invasive complementary biomarker.

papers.title: Acute intermittent carotid body stimulations induce long-term facilitation of respiratory-cardiovascular coupling in rats.
papers.summary: Using the in situ working heart-brainstem preparation in rats, four brief intermittent carotid body stimulations with sodium cyanide produced a prolonged (>20 min) increase in inspiratory and late expiratory respiratory-modulated sympathetic activity, Traube-Hering waves, and perfusion pressure, effects prevented by carotid sinus denervation. The findings indicate acute intermittent carotid body activation induces long-term facilitation of respiratory-cardiovascular coupling relevant to hypertension pathogenesis.

papers.title: Multimodal EEG-fNIRS complexity analysis can reveal the neurovascular coupling change with aging.
papers.summary: Simultaneous EEG-fNIRS with nonlinear entropy analysis in 20 young and 20 older adults across four cognitive tasks revealed task-specific age-related differences in neural and hemodynamic complexity and in cross-modal entropy measures, suggesting neurovascular coupling changes with aging reflect dynamic reorganization rather than uniform enhancement or impairment.

papers.title: Associations between circadian-related behaviors and light exposure and depressive and anxiety symptoms among college students: A cross-sectional study of 10, 630 students from 4 universities.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional survey of 10,630 Chinese university students, evening chronotype, social jetlag, nighttime artificial light exposure, and pre-sleep phone use were associated with higher PHQ-9 and GAD-7 scores, while daytime sunlight exposure was associated with lower scores. Isotopic substitution models suggested replacing 30 min of pre-sleep phone use with sunlight or sleep was associated with lower symptom scores.

papers.title: Role of External Factors in the Severity of Dissociation Experienced by Treatment- Resistant Depression Patients Following Esketamine Administration.
papers.summary: This case series describes two treatment-resistant depression patients on esketamine nasal spray who experienced unusually severe dissociation (CADSS 27 and 21) coinciding with recent stressors—sleep deprivation from newborn caregiving and a trauma-related social media trigger. The authors suggest assessing recent stressors or routine changes before each esketamine session may help predict severe dissociation risk.

papers.title: Multiscale EEG network alterations in adolescents with depressive symptoms: static-dynamic connectivity, topological features, and exploratory scalp-level network hubs.
papers.summary: Resting-state EEG from 96 adolescents with depressive symptoms and 154 controls was analyzed with adaptive-threshold multiscale networks, revealing theta-band static hyperconnectivity along midline prefrontal-central connections, reduced dynamic transition flexibility in prefrontal systems, and topological vulnerability of right prefrontal nodes (Fp2, F4), with overlap to exploratory neuromodulation hub projections.

papers.title: Beyond Exploration: Heightened Recent Reward Reliance and Midfrontal Sensitivity to Outcome Differences in ADHD
papers.summary: Using a restless four-armed bandit task with EEG in 23 adults with self-reported ADHD and 27 controls, this study tested whether ADHD alters the exploration-exploitation trade-off and reward-history weighting. Exploration rates, performance, and neural differentiation between explore and exploit did not differ, but ADHD participants showed stronger reliance on the immediately preceding outcome (repeat after high reward, switch after low reward) and greater slow-wave (<2 Hz) midfrontal sensitivity to unsigned payoff changes from 280–568 ms.

papers.title: Oral breathing and its dental and cognitive implications: a structured narrative review with a pediatric focus.
papers.summary: This structured narrative review synthesized 23 primary studies on habitual oral breathing in children and found consistent associations with malocclusion, altered craniofacial morphology, and oral disease, alongside associations with reduced working memory, attention difficulties, altered brain oxygenation, and sleep-disordered breathing. It proposes a hypothesis-generating framework linking dental and cognitive outcomes, possibly via disrupted nasal nitric oxide signaling, while noting that no study examined both outcome domains in the same participants.

papers.title: Perioperative esketamine and postoperative sleep quality: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 23 randomized trials (2868 participants) found that perioperative esketamine improved postoperative sleep quality on days 1, 2, 3, and 7 and reduced postoperative sleep disturbance incidence on days 1-3, with no benefit at 1 month, and also lowered postoperative pain and depression scores. Benefits were offset by a markedly increased risk of drowsiness (RR 12.64).

papers.title: Symptom-Level Comorbidity Patterns Between Depression and Internet Gaming Disorder Among Adolescents: Evidence from Longitudinal Network Analysis with Gender Considerations.
papers.summary: Using two-wave cross-lagged panel network analysis in 538 adolescents, this study found that depressive symptoms consistently predicted later Internet gaming disorder symptoms, with no reverse cross-disorder pathways, and identified suicidal ideation and psychomotor symptoms as bridge symptoms. Sleep problems showed moderate outgoing expected influence, and network patterns were broadly similar but not identical across genders.

papers.title: How does circadian preference relate to post-traumatic stress and depressive symptoms in adolescents? A moderating role of gender.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional survey of 9305 Chinese secondary-school adolescents, latent profile analysis identified three circadian profiles (Morning-Coordinated, Intermediate-Stable, Evening-Fluctuating), with the Evening-Fluctuating profile showing markedly elevated odds of comorbid PTSS and depressive symptoms, isolated depression, and isolated PTSS. Morning affect was protective while eveningness and distinctness were risk factors, and these associations were consistently stronger in girls.

papers.title: Habitual sleep duration and spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage: a prospective UK Biobank cohort study with supporting hospital-based neurosurgical data.
papers.summary: In a prospective UK Biobank cohort of 314,236 participants (1,387 incident spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhages), both short and long habitual sleep were associated with higher sICH risk, with stronger associations for long sleep (adjusted HR 1.55), supported by a hospital-based case-control analysis and U-shaped dose-response. Inflammatory markers neither explained nor reliably modified these associations.

papers.title: Exploring Data Augmentation for Stroke Severity Prediction: How Generative AI Enhances EEG Signal Classification
papers.summary: This study evaluated generative data augmentation for EEG-based stroke severity classification using recordings from 50 stroke patients, comparing SMOTE, ADASYN, WGAN, and WGAN-GP within a hybrid pipeline of preprocessing, statistical/frequency feature extraction, feature reduction, and multiple classifiers. The best result was 72% accuracy with SelectKBest feature selection, SVM, and WGAN-GP augmentation, indicating that generative augmentation can improve classification on small, imbalanced clinical EEG datasets.

papers.title: Side-to-side and other complex head movements as ictal signs in epilepsy: A video-EEG case series and review of literature.
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.summary: In a retrospective video-EEG series of 17 patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy (631 seizures, 201 with complex head movements), ictal side-to-side and other complex head movements occurred across heterogeneous epileptogenic zones and lacked localizing or lateralizing value, likely reflecting seizure propagation.

papers.title: Optimizing aprocitentan dosing in elderly Chinese patients with resistant hypertension: a PBPK/PD-circadian rhythm modeling study.
papers.summary: This study developed and validated an integrated PBPK/PD-circadian rhythm model for aprocitentan and extrapolated it to elderly Chinese patients with resistant hypertension, predicting a 20.6% higher steady-state AUC than in healthy elderly Caucasians (52.5% higher with mild hepatic impairment). Simulations identified 6.25 mg once daily and midday (12:00-13:00) administration as candidate regimens, with predicted systolic/diastolic BP reductions of about 13.0/9.0 mmHg.

papers.title: Restorative free time and psychological distress among employed family caregivers of individuals with cognitive impairment: a cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional analysis of 210 employed family caregivers of individuals with cognitive impairment, caregivers with less than 1 h/day of restorative free time and those sleeping less than 6 h/day had a significantly higher prevalence of psychological distress (Kessler 6), whereas working hours and caregiving duration were not significantly associated after adjustment. Limited restorative free time is proposed as a potential marker of psychological distress, though the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference.

papers.title: Ethical Risks and Governance of Consumer Electroencephalography-Based Neurotechnology: Qualitative Interview Study With Expert Stakeholders
papers.summary: Conducted semi-structured interviews with 19 expert stakeholders across research, clinical practice, engineering, industry, ethics, law, and regulation to examine ethical, regulatory, and data governance challenges of consumer EEG neurotechnology. Reflexive thematic analysis yielded five themes spanning regulatory boundaries, evidential credibility and claims-related harm, neurodata privacy and inference, layered accountability, and global equity, concluding that governance duties must be explicitly allocated across multiple actors and lifecycle stages.

papers.title: Opsoclonus-myoclonus-ataxia syndrome in an elderly female: A video-based case report and literature review.
papers.summary: Reports an 81-year-old woman who developed opsoclonus, myoclonus, ataxia, behavioral changes, and sleep disturbance, diagnosed with idiopathic OMAS after unremarkable laboratory and imaging workup and no tumor detected on follow-up. She improved markedly with steroid immunotherapy plus clonazepam and gabapentin, with no recurrence or malignancy at two-year follow-up, accompanied by video documentation and a literature review.

papers.title: Association between an improved positioning management strategy and non-incisional low back pain and sleep quality in patients undergoing modified radical mastectomy for breast cancer: a retrospective cohort study.
papers.summary: Single-center retrospective cohort of women undergoing mastectomy for breast cancer comparing an improved perioperative positioning management strategy with usual care. Improved positioning was associated with significantly lower non-incisional low back pain (beta = -0.711, P < .001) with greater reductions at 48 and 72 h and higher postoperative sleep quality, without increases in drainage volume, seroma, or flap ischemia/necrosis.

papers.title: Quantifying Academic Risk Factors for Student Depression Using WHO Frameworks: Odds Ratios, SHAP Explainability, and Tipping Point Analysis
papers.summary: Using data from 27,880 Indian university students and an interpretability-focused approach (logistic regression odds ratios, Random Forest/XGBoost importance, SHAP values, tipping point analysis), the study found academic pressure to be the dominant depression risk factor (OR = 2.271; RF importance = 0.481), while study satisfaction (OR = 0.796) and sleep duration (OR = 0.835) were protective; ensemble models reached ~77–78% accuracy and AUC 0.845.

papers.title: Effect of neurofeedback-assisted mindfulness training on migraine severity, associated disability, sleep quality, and emotional distress: protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: This protocol describes a randomized, parallel-group controlled trial of 66 adults with medium-to-high-frequency episodic migraine (5–14 monthly migraine days) testing a 12-week home-based neurofeedback-assisted mindfulness training program (Muse EEG headband, 60 sessions) plus standard care versus standard care alone, with monthly migraine days as the primary outcome and secondary outcomes including MIDAS, HIT-6, actigraphy/PSQI sleep measures, quality of life, and mood.

papers.title: Prevalence of Overweight and Obesity and Their Associations With Screen Time and Other Behavioral Factors Among Adolescents in the United Arab Emirates.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional study of 688 adolescents aged 14-18 years in the UAE found a combined overweight/obesity prevalence of 39.8% (27.3% overweight, 12.5% obese). In multivariable analysis overweight/obesity was associated with male sex (AOR 1.636), family history of obesity (AOR 2.014), frequent eating when not hungry or bored (AOR 1.884), and no days of >=60 minutes/day out-of-school moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (AOR 1.896), while recreational screen time was not significant in regression.

papers.title: Cogwheel Rigidity in Subacute Combined Degeneration Unresponsive to Vitamin B12 Therapy.
papers.summary: Case study of a 62-year-old woman with subacute combined degeneration and pernicious anemia whose cogwheel rigidity persisted despite three years of monthly vitamin B12 injections and normalized B12 levels, alongside hyposmia, ptosis, pronator drift, hyperreflexia, and bilateral Hoffman and Babinski signs. The authors propose extension of demyelination into reticulospinal and rubrospinal tracts or coexisting subclinical parkinsonism, and recommend evaluating for parkinsonism in SCD.

papers.title: Cardiovascular Health Promotion for US Veterans: Current State, Gaps, and Strategies: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
authors: American Heart Association Council on Lifestyle and Cardiometabolic Health; Council on Arteriosclerosis, Thrombosis and Vascular Biology; Council on Cardiovascular and Stroke Nursing; Council on Cardiovascular Radiology and Intervention; Council on Clinical Cardiology; and Council on Quality of Care and Outcomes Research
papers.summary: This AHA scientific statement evaluates cardiovascular health among US veterans using the Life's Essential 8 framework expanded to include mental health and substance use, reviewing guideline recommendations, barriers, and major VA programs across domains. It reports that veterans receiving VA care often achieve outcomes equal to or better than non-VA counterparts, reflecting strengths in coordinated team-based care, while identifying remaining opportunities to improve lifestyle behaviors, metabolic health, and sleep disorder management.

papers.title: Aviation Medicine and Cardiovascular Assessment of Aircrew: A European Society of Cardiology-Aligned Review of Integrating International Civil Aviation Organization, European Union Aviation Safety Agency, Federal Aviation Administration, and Turkish Directorate General of Civil Aviation Aeromedical Standards.
papers.summary: This review summarizes aeromedical cardiovascular assessment of aircrew, integrating ICAO, EASA, FAA, and Turkish DGCA standards with European Society of Cardiology guidance across conditions including hypertension, coronary syndromes, arrhythmias, valvular disease, and devices. It reports that preserved ventricular function, low arrhythmic/thromboembolic risk, stable treatment, and adequate exercise capacity generally support certification, whereas uncontrolled hypertension, reduced ejection fraction, malignant arrhythmias, or severe valvular/aortic disease usually preclude it.

papers.title: Can COVID-19 Cause Acute Psychosis in Pediatric Patients? A Case Report.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 14-year-old female with no psychiatric history who developed acute psychosis with visual hallucinations two weeks after COVID-19 infection, improving on chlorpromazine and returning to school over two months. It highlights that COVID-19-associated acute psychosis, though rare, can occur in pediatric patients and that clinicians should test for COVID-19 and consider organic causes in new-onset psychosis.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
